Hi Karthik and Vanessa —

Thanks for the SOW draft. Two quick items from our side:

1) Our legal wants the committed tranche to be locked to calendarized GPU slots (we need predictability for a regulatory audit).
2) Your sales portal showed "waitlist" for additional burst capacity in July — our engineering team has a rollout that depends on those extra slots.

Megan — appreciate the heads up and the calendar. Short answer: the base SOW secures the committed tranche (reserved GPUs), but we do allow preemption rules at the tranche/bucket level when the fleet hits sustained congestion.

Options we can offer:
- Formal priority: upgrade to a "guaranteed lane" (higher commit, different pricing) — blocks preemption except for force-majeure.
- Waitlist mitigation: guaranteed monthly burst windows (2 x 4-hour blocks) with notice — cheaper than full upgrade.
- Credits: if preempted outside windows, AuroraPulse receives service credits tied to SLA.

I'm looping Marcus to provide feasibility on the July burst windows and whether we can hard-claim those hours against the current commit.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Team —

Readout after a quick capacity check: we have three competing signals in July. Two large reserved deals (one closing next week) plus several existing tranches already scheduled. Current fleet utilization projections for the affected AZ/cluster (us-west-2a) show a 92% median utilization window during the July 12–20 timeframe.

Key constraints: 1) GPUs assigned to reserved capacity are pinned; 2) Waitlist/burst currently implemented as opportunistic preemption-tolerant slots; 3) We do have a small pool for "guaranteed burst" but it is not unlimited.

Proposal for arbitration (I recommend Vanessa lead):
- Priority matrix (quick):
  * Tier 1: Legal SLA customers with explicit "no-preempt" lane (higher price).
  * Tier 2: Active signed reserved commitments (like AuroraPulse base SOW) — guaranteed base capacity but subject to tranche-level preemption rules unless upgraded.
  * Tier 3: Waitlist/burst requests — offer scheduled windows or credits.

- For AuroraPulse specifically: we can commit 2 guaranteed 4-hour burst windows in July (July 13 and July 18, 10:00–14:00 PT) if they accept a minor amendment to the SOW (adds $X/month). Without an amendment, their request remains on the waitlist and could be preempted by the larger deal closing next week.

- If Ops approves, I'll reserve the burst window and mark the reconcile action in INF-4821 (linked). Otherwise we escalate pricing/seat to avoid conflict.

Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachment: tranche-allocation-proposal.xlsx

Folks — quick decision required to avoid losing AuroraPulse to the larger reserved deal. Summary and decision options below:

Summary:
- AuroraPulse has a signed base SOW that secures their committed tranche but not guaranteed burst windows.
- A larger reserved deal (legal has "no-preempt") is likely to claim additional capacity in July.
- Marcus can guarantee two 4-hour burst windows if AuroraPulse accepts an SOW amendment (price delta ~6% of the monthly commit).

Decision options (pick one, I'll execute and notify legal / billing):
A) Approve the SOW amendment and reserve the two July burst windows for AuroraPulse. Outcome: prevents preemption for those windows, maintains overall fairness.
B) Hold to current SOW (no amendment). Outcome: AuroraPulse stays on waitlist; risk of preemption during peak July window; offer SLA credits if preempted.
C) Offer temporary higher-priority lane (Tier 1) at premium pricing — only if sales converts within 48 hours. Outcome: blocks larger-deal preemption entirely.

Recommendation: A) — keep the customer happy, minimal revenue upside, avoids legal friction. Marcus, confirm you can block the windows once we get sign-off. Laura, confirm Ops will mark the units as reserved so they are not reallocated. Karthik, please draft a short amendment and send to Megan for signature (DocuSign link in related_links).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
